analysis:
Reviewed all nine supplied analyses and the available source replay; no independently supported security regression was established. Replay is incomplete (35 source units omitted), so earlier conclusions were not treated as proof.
Verified changes: ClusterSetupWizardLiveOperations.swift:618,625 delegates coordinator-aware assistant discovery to readAutomatic. ClusterPublicModels.swift:47–62 validates singleton assistant policies and commits inventory, depth, verification and evidence identity; :151–157 restricts lookup to a qualifying artifact with tensor-parallel eligibility. DistributedInstalledNativeStart.swift:32–40 and ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts.swift:296–302 use the same assistant-inclusive resource-policy digest. Release facts now default to current declarations (ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts+Release.swift:54). ClusterApprovalAttachment.swift:139–140 retains configuration validation before attachment; its changed comments do not establish additional enforcement.
These interactions affect model/output integrity (T-007/T-027), serving/build qualification and authorization (T-052/T-053/T-054), availability (A-018), and the distinction between declared evidence and correct computation (T-056). A declaration or evidence hash is not itself coordinator authorization. No replayed change directly modifies hop encryption, credential custody, billing, media storage, privileged helpers, or T-041 cache isolation/storage controls.
Material unresolved contracts require further review: verify ClusterConfiguration.swift:168–176 enforces exact assistant-policy equality; inspect ClusterPlacementTensorAssistantSelection.readAutomatic/discoveryMode and native launch plumbing to confirm discovered, quoted and executed assistants match the committed inventory and resources. Reconcile the publicTrafficLine eligibility change with independent placement qualification, and verify declarationOverride has no product setter. The relevant implementation and test additions are not replayed sufficiently to resolve these questions. Their absence is a coverage limit, not evidence of missing controls or a bypass.
